New York Yankees.text: The team began in 1903 as the New York Highlanders and was renamed the Yankees in 1913.
New York Yankees.evidence: The team was founded in 1903 when Frank Farrell and Bill Devery purchased the franchise rights to the defunct Baltimore Orioles and used them to establish the New York Highlanders. The Highlanders were renamed the Yankees in 1913.

St. Louis Cardinals.text: Their manager and owner Branch Rickey invented baseball's farm system.
St. Louis Cardinals.evidence: Notable Cardinals achievements include manager/owner Branch Rickey's invention of the farm system, Rogers Hornsby's two batting Triple Crowns, Dizzy Dean's 30-win season in 1934, Stan Musial's 17 MLB and 29 NL records, Bob Gibson's 1.12 earned run average (ERA) in 1968, Whitey Herzog's Whiteyball dynasty of the 1980s, Mark McGwire's single-season home run record in 1998, the 2011 championship team's unprecedented comebacks, and Albert Pujols’ 700th home run.

Los Angeles Dodgers.text: As the Brooklyn Dodgers, they broke baseball's color line in 1947 with Jackie Robinson's debut.
Los Angeles Dodgers.evidence: The Dodgers broke the baseball color line in 1947 with the debut of Jackie Robinson, the first African American to play in the Major Leagues since 1884.

Athletics.text: After Philadelphia, the franchise moved to Kansas City in 1954, Oakland in 1967 and West Sacramento in 2025.
Athletics.evidence: The Philadelphia Athletics were a Major League Baseball team that played in Philadelphia from 1901 to 1954, when they moved to Kansas City, Missouri, and became the Kansas City Athletics. After another move to Oakland, California, in 1967, they became the Oakland Athletics. In 2025, the team moved to West Sacramento, California, as the Athletics, and plans ultimately to move to the Las Vegas metropolitan area.

Boston Red Sox.text: Their 86-year title drought was dubbed the "Curse of the Bambino", after the sale of Babe Ruth to the Yankees.
Boston Red Sox.evidence: However, they then went into one of the longest championship droughts in baseball history, dubbed the "Curse of the Bambino" after its alleged inception due to the Red Sox' sale of star player Babe Ruth to the rival New York Yankees two years after their World Series championship in 1918. The Sox endured an 86-year wait before the team's sixth World Series championship in 2004.

San Francisco Giants.text: The franchise has more wins than any other in Major League Baseball history.
San Francisco Giants.evidence: The franchise is one of the oldest and most successful in professional baseball, with more wins than any other franchise in Major League Baseball history.

Cincinnati Reds.text: An earlier Cincinnati club was expelled from the National League for refusing to give up beer sales and Sunday baseball.
Cincinnati Reds.evidence: In 1876, Cincinnati became one of the charter members of the new National League (NL), but the club ran afoul of league organizer and longtime president William Hulbert for selling beer during games and renting out its ballpark on Sundays. ... On October 6, 1880, however, seven of the eight team owners adopted a pledge to ban both beer and Sunday baseball at the regular league meeting in December. Only Cincinnati president W. H. Kennett refused to sign the pledge, so the other owners preemptively expelled Cincinnati from the league for violating the new rules even though they were not yet in effect.

Pittsburgh Pirates.text: Bill Mazeroski's 1960 walk-off is the only time Game 7 of a World Series has ended on a home run.
Pittsburgh Pirates.evidence: The club won the 1960 World Series against the New York Yankees on a walk-off home run by Bill Mazeroski, the only time that Game 7 of the World Series has ever ended with a home run.

Detroit Tigers.text: In 1984 they won 35 of their first 40 games on the way to the championship.
Detroit Tigers.evidence: The franchise record for most wins in a season is 104 in 1984, when the club won 35 of its first 40 games en route to the World Series championship.

Atlanta Braves.text: They are the only MLB franchise to win the World Series in three different home cities.
Atlanta Braves.evidence: The Braves are the only Major League Baseball franchise to have won the World Series in three different home cities.
